Definition: second person singular present imperative of G1510; be thou; also ἔστωσαν, third person of the same; let them be:--be.
BiblicalUsage: Éstō is the word for 'let it be' — the imperative of the verb to be. It is the word of command and of consent: 'let your yea be yea', 'let every man be swift to hear', 'let it be the hidden man of the heart'. The form turns being into an instruction.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that éstō is a word to obey: it tells me what must be, and leaves the doing to me.
